method: Directed non-exhaustive primary-source search; substantive summaries only. No foreign PDFs, HTML corpus or full-text extracts persisted. PDF bytes were fetched in memory to compute hashes; those hashes are in PRIMARY_FETCH_METADATA958.json. A fetch/hash is not a claim of complete reading.

sources.title: Complete Entropic Inequalities for Quantum Markov Chains
sources.proofs_read: Comparison proof and double-integral entropy remainder in those lemmas
sources.not_read: The entire paper and its applications
sources.assessment: BKM comparison and entropy integration are prior ingredients, not manuscript innovations.

sources.title: Reduction criterion of separability and limits for a class of protocols of entanglement distillation
sources.statements_read: Section III equations 8-11; Appendix A equations 59-65
sources.proofs_read: Positive-map reduction argument and Choi/flip calculation establishing decomposability
sources.assessment: SEP and PPT imply unilateral reduction by known methods; reduction can include NPT states.

sources.title: A Schmidt number for density matrices
sources.statements_read: Schmidt number definition, Theorem 1, Proposition 1, Lemma 3
sources.proofs_read: Theorem 1 positive-map separation proof and associated lemma discussion
sources.not_read: Every isotropic-state construction or additivity example
sources.assessment: Schmidt hierarchy/positive-map witnessing are prior; manuscript order implication was also reconstructed directly by whitening pure components.

sources.title: Conditional contraction coefficients and their applications to quantum networks
sources.statements_read: Section 2.2 definitions 1-2, Section 3.2 Lemmas 4-5 and Theorem 2, Corollaries 2-3, Section 3.3 equations 3.63-3.66; Section 4.1 discussion citing Gao-Zhao
sources.proofs_read: Lemma 4, Theorem 2 and Lemma 5 arguments in the relevant passages
sources.not_read: Full conditional-equivalence Theorem 1 proof, network applications and all appendices
sources.assessment: Separates actual-product MI, equal-reference-marginal pairs and conditional divergence. Its displayed examples do not optimize the separable coefficient. Beating 0.2881 does not resolve equality or strict separation of its optimized coefficients.

sources.title: On contraction coefficients, partial orders and approximation of capacities for quantum channels
sources.statements_read: Lemma 3.12 and equations 3.50-3.55; generalized-depolarization fixed-state discussion
sources.proofs_read: Lemma 3.12 is a citation to an antecedent, not a full proof here. The review independently reconstructed the qubit bound using Bloch BKM eigenvalues.
sources.not_read: Full cited Hiai-Ruskai proof and whole article
sources.assessment: Ordinary qubit relative-entropy contraction lambda squared is known.

sources.title: Hilbert's projective metric in quantum information theory
sources.statements_read: Appendix B equations 94-97 and adjacent PPT discussion
sources.proofs_read: Projective-diameter lower/upper construction and ordinary norm contraction calculation
sources.not_read: Whole main text and proofs of general projective-metric theorems
sources.assessment: Same replacement family, different metric and global replacement in its bipartite discussion; does not supply the sharp actual-marginal MI optimization inspected here.

sources.title: Entanglement-Assisted Classical Capacity of Noisy Quantum Channels
sources.proofs_read: Superdense-coding/teleportation matching-bound explanation in that discussion
sources.assessment: Depolarizing output spectrum and unbounded assisted advantage are old. Manuscript's comparison to a newly sharp separable retention denominator is narrower than a capacity discovery.

sources.version: Published 2023 Phys. Rev. Research 5, 033214; also inspected arXiv 2206.05247v1 (2022)
sources.title: Quantum networks boosted by entanglement with a control system
sources.statements_read: Published pp. 1-4, especially page 4 equation 6 and partial-information-erasure discussion
sources.proofs_read: Local channel/Kraus and retained-control distinctions in those passages; not full protocol proofs
sources.assessment: Published equation 6 does contain partial pure resets. arXiv v1 equation 6 instead labels Kraus operators, so the published version matters. The manuscript's DOI citation is correct.
sources.hash_limitation: Direct PDF hash fetch returned 403; web tool successfully displayed the published PDF. arXiv v1 hash is recorded separately and is not substituted for published bytes.

sources.title: Quantum dynamics with stochastic reset
sources.assessment: Renewal integral is prior. Its reset-to-initial-state specialization is distinct from choosing a reset from an unknown channel input; the manuscript correctly fixes the target.

sources.title: Spectral properties of simple classical and quantum reset processes
sources.statements_read: Section V.1 equations 52-68 and coherent Hamiltonian specialization 71-74
sources.proofs_read: Jump-operator construction, trace-zero mode shift and stationary-mode derivation in those passages
sources.not_read: All classical examples or metastability analysis
sources.assessment: Fixed pure reset generator and uniform spectral shift are prior. No exact constrained MI theorem was found in the inspected sections.

sources.title: Tight Entropy Contraction of Generalized Quantum Depolarization
sources.statements_read: Propositions 1.1/2.3, Definition 3.1, Proposition 3.2, Definition 3.7, Corollary 3.8, Theorem 3.13, Remark 3.14 and Section 4.1; confirmed PDF abstract/introduction
sources.proofs_read: Section 2.2 BKM proof of ratio bounds; index proof and derivation of Corollary 3.8 in inspected passages
sources.not_read: Every theorem/appendix or an independent correctness audit of this paper
sources.assessment: Directly relevant omitted antecedent. Its contraction is measured relative to a fixed-point expectation E(rho), giving tau tensor rho_R for a replacer, whereas sharp957 compares the actual input/output products of marginals. Its fixed-reference bounds do not directly prove the claimed separable sharp MI formula. Comparison should be added; no worldwide priority certification follows.
